adjudication_summary.description: Descriptive workflow statistic; NOT reported in the paper and NOT a post-adjudication agreement measurement. Each field counts round-0 disagreements between annotator A (Ginsberg) and annotator B (Moster) reconciled into the consensus by the two-round diff-and-revise protocol (which ended in a byte-identical SHA-256 endorsement). Units differ by tier and tier 1-3 are NESTED (tier N includes tier <N) -- DO NOT SUM. See iaa_report.json::_note.

tier1_disagreements_reconciled.description: Cluster-aligned code-point edit ops between the two round-0 tier-1 (consonantal) projections, over all verses. Reproducible from the two committed projections alone.

tier2_disagreements_reconciled.description: Same at tier 2 (+nikkud); INCLUDES the tier-1 consonantal edits -- not disjoint from tier1.

tier3_disagreements_reconciled.description: Same at tier 3 (full text); INCLUDES the tier-1 and tier-2 edits -- not disjoint.

tier4_disagreements_reconciled.description: Unmatched tier-4 detections (FP+FN) under the paper's §5.1 headline exact-match config (UXLC-anchored, canonicalised; 4 unalignable records dropped). Same frame as tier4.f1_mean.

cer_vs_consensus_b.description: Annotator B's round-0 transcription vs the adjudicated consensus reference, per DRAFT_v4 §5.2. NOT a bidirectional A-vs-B agreement figure and NOT an independent human-vs-reference baseline: the consensus is A's round-1 revision, byte-identical to B's round-2 endorsement, so it is not independent of either annotator. The paper reports no bidirectional tier-1/2/3 CER; the word does not appear in it. Renamed from bidirectional_cer_mean 2026-07-10 (B3).
